solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Radar perhaps picked up circuit in start of descent over capital

indicators.note: in a down clue, something picked up is lifted so it reads from bottom to top

parts.note: a lap is one circuit of a track
taken as written

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the following word is taken

parts.note: Rome is the capital of Italy

explanation.surface: An aircraft's radar tracks it circling in the early stage of its descent above a capital city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' in a down clue just puts D above ROME.
explanation.definitionFit: Radar reads the same forwards and backwards, so it is an example of such a word; 'perhaps' marks the example.

clue.text: You and I run away from Border Terrier — or what he might be carrying?

parts.note: the speaker and the listener together are 'we'

indicators.note: the letter for run departs from the border word, leaving the rest

parts.note: an apron is a border or edging strip, as the apron of a stage or airfield
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: A pair flee from a Border Terrier dog, wondering what it might have in its jaws.
explanation.walkthrough: A Terrier is also a member of the Territorial Army, Britain's reserve force; 'he' is that soldier, whose kit includes a gun.
explanation.definitionFit: A Territorial soldier carries arms, so a rifle or other arm is what he might have with him.

clue.text: Rum served by saloon, perhaps in poor island

indicators.note: the vehicle sits inside the word for poor

parts.note: poor quality means bad
a saloon is a type of car, hence 'perhaps'

explanation.surface: Rum being poured in a bar, perhaps on some impoverished island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'saloon' looks like a bar serving drinks, but it is a car.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a well-known brand of rum from the Caribbean, so the spirit names it.

clue.text: Bird reported little row

indicators.note: reported speech is heard rather than read, so the phrase is said aloud

parts.note: a wee tier is a small row, Scots 'wee' meaning little

explanation.surface: A bird was spotted, and a minor quarrel was reported.
explanation.walkthrough: 'row' suggests a quarrel, but here it is a tier, as of seats.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a small migratory songbird with a white rump.

clue.text: Having enough power to overthrow an island

indicators.note: to overthrow is to turn over, so the word is read from the bottom up

parts.note: having the power to do something is being able

explanation.surface: Someone strong enough to overthrow an island's rulers.
explanation.walkthrough: Napoleon, who overthrew governments, was exiled to this island, which gives the surface its edge.
explanation.definitionFit: The Mediterranean isle off Tuscany where Napoleon spent his first exile.

clue.text: Stock form of communication?

parts.note: 'Stock' reads as standard or clichéd, but means livestock: the way cattle call out

explanation.surface: A query about a hackneyed way of getting a message across.
explanation.walkthrough: Livestock are 'stock', so their way of communicating is the sound cows make.
explanation.definitionFit: Cattle are farm stock, and lowing is how they communicate with each other.

clue.text: Do this to opposition to get on

definitions.text: Do this to opposition to get on

parts.words: Do this to opposition to get on
parts.note: emptying the word 'opposition' of its middle letters leaves only its first and last, O and N

explanation.surface: Advice on dealing with opponents in order to make progress.
explanation.walkthrough: To empty a word in crosswords is to remove its interior, leaving the outside letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To clear out or empty a place is to leave it, and emptying that word leaves just its ends.

clue.text: Cumbrian market town needing fruit in reserve

parts.note: an apple is a common fruit
something put by is kept in reserve

explanation.surface: A northern English market town that needs fruit held back for later.
explanation.walkthrough: Appleby-in-Westmorland, in Cumbria in north-west England, is famed for its horse fair.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a small town in the Eden valley of Cumbria with a long-established market charter.

clue.text: Time to avoid one hot planet, almost around orbital apex?

indicators.note: the letters are moved around into a new order
the word hot must do without the time letter

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: the word planet is cut short by its final letter

explanation.surface: A spacecraft dodging a scorching planet as it nearly circles the top of its orbit.
explanation.walkthrough: HO (hot without T), I and PLANE (planet almost) are shuffled by 'around'.
explanation.definitionFit: The point in an orbit farthest from the Sun is its extreme, a technical term for an orbital apex.

clue.text: Food and fuel endlessly added onto rent

indicators.note: the second piece is attached after the first

parts.note: a rent is a tear or split

indicators.note: the fuel word loses its last letter

parts.note: peat is dug and burned as fuel

explanation.surface: Bills for food and heating keep piling on top of the rent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rent' looks like housing cost but is a noun meaning a tear.
explanation.definitionFit: A dried, halved pea is a staple ingredient for soups, so it is a food.

clue.text: Slowly answer foreign soldier in trouble

indicators.note: the two letters sit inside the word for trouble

parts.note: ado is fuss or trouble
a GI is an American soldier, foreign from a British setter's view

explanation.surface: A slow reply comes from an American soldier in difficulty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Slowly' looks like an adverb on 'answer' but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: This Italian musical direction tells performers to play at a slow, leisurely tempo.

clue.text: Projection about duke that's close to the bone

indicators.note: the projection wraps around the duke's letter

parts.note: a tenon is a projecting tongue of wood fitting a mortise

explanation.surface: A projecting remark about a duke that's rather risqué.
explanation.walkthrough: 'close to the bone' suggests near-the-knuckle humour, but is literal: it joins muscle to bone.
explanation.definitionFit: This band of tough fibrous tissue attaches muscle to bone, so it lies right next to it.

clue.text: One could be up for this treat given time

definitions.text: One could be up for this

parts.note: to dress a wound is to treat it
an age is a long period of time

explanation.surface: Someone keen on a treat, if given time.
explanation.walkthrough: A rider in the saddle is said to be 'up', so 'up for this' means mounted to compete in it.
explanation.definitionFit: This equestrian discipline has a mounted rider guide the horse through precise movements.

clue.text: Drunk best sake in mixed drinks

indicators.note: drunk means the letters are reeling into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone drunk on the finest sake as part of a mix of drinks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drunk' looks like a description of the drinker but scrambles BEST SAKE IN.
explanation.definitionFit: This pub drink is lager and cider combined, often with blackcurrant: a mixture.

clue.text: Shivering, ropy little sibling getting heartburn

indicators.note: shivering means the letters are shaken up

parts.note: sis is a short form of sister, a sibling

explanation.surface: A trembling, weedy younger sister suffering from indigestion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'little' signals the clipped form, not a younger child.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the medical term for the burning chest pain from stomach acid.

clue.text: Comic piece found in free introduction to adult hotline

indicators.note: letters set free are loosed into a new arrangement
only the first letter of the word adult is used

explanation.surface: A funny item found among free trial offers for an adult chat line.
explanation.walkthrough: A comic opera by Gilbert and Sullivan, the Victorian duo of light operetta.
explanation.definitionFit: This Gilbert and Sullivan work about a fairy is a comic opera, a humorous stage piece.

clue.text: French leave genuine French city, cutting east then north

indicators.note: the compass letters are cut out of the joined words

parts.note: genuine means true
Nancy is a city in Lorraine

explanation.surface: Taking unofficial time off in a real French city, travelling east then north.
explanation.walkthrough: 'French leave' is a British idiom for absence without permission.
explanation.definitionFit: Skipping school or work without permission is an idiomatic sense of taking unauthorised absence.

clue.text: Struggle to study before exam

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece comes above the second

parts.note: to con is an old verb meaning to study or learn
a test is an exam

explanation.surface: A student struggling to revise ahead of an exam.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Struggle' reads as a verb but works as a noun here.
explanation.definitionFit: A fight or competition for victory is a struggle between rivals.

clue.text: Femme fatale about to stop a text message that is upsetting

indicators.note: the word for about plugs the middle of the message

parts.note: LOL, 'laughing out loud', is a common text message
re means about or concerning

indicators.note: in a down clue, upsetting turns the letters upside down

parts.note: ie is the abbreviation of id est, 'that is'

explanation.surface: A seductive woman is about to stop sending a hurtful text.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upsetting' looks like an adjective for the message but turns IE into EI.
explanation.definitionFit: In German legend this Rhine siren lured boatmen to their doom, the archetypal seductress.

clue.text: A better place to go on playing polo? Sure

indicators.note: playing means the letters are in play, rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a better spot is going to the polo match, and is told yes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'place to go' is a euphemism for a lavatory; 'better' signals 'super'. A superloo is an automated public toilet.
explanation.definitionFit: A superior public toilet is literally a better lavatory, a place one goes.

clue.text: Possibly odd Tyneside sports location shortly to be erected

indicators.note: in a down clue, erecting sets the letters upright, reading upwards

parts.note: Tyneside is in the North East of England, NE

indicators.note: the venue word is cut short by its last letter

parts.note: a venue is where sport is played

explanation.surface: A strange plan for a sports ground in Newcastle to be built soon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shortly' means soon in the surface but trims VENUE; NEVENU is then reversed.
explanation.definitionFit: Odd numbers are not even, so 'odd' is one example of the sense; 'possibly' marks it.

clue.text: Calling on eastern European to cut grass

indicators.note: the two letters cut into the word for grass

parts.note: to grass on someone is to inform, or sing

explanation.surface: Visiting an Eastern European to mow the lawn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grass' looks like the lawn but is the slang verb to inform.
explanation.definitionFit: To call on a friend is to visit them, which can be put as going to see them.

clue.text: Rough and coarse bird, outwardly gaudy

parts.note: the shag is a seabird of the cormorant family

indicators.note: only the outside letters of gaudy are taken

explanation.surface: A harsh, coarse-feathered bird with a loud exterior.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coarse' seems to describe the bird but belongs to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Hair or fur that is long, rough and unkempt is described with this word.

clue.text: Danger sign in advice to turn oneself in?

definitions.meaning: a signal fire or light warning of danger
read as three words, the advice is to become a convict, 'con'

explanation.surface: A warning signal hidden in advice to surrender to the police.
explanation.walkthrough: CON is crossword shorthand for a convict.
explanation.definitionFit: A fire or light set up high as a warning is a signal of danger.

clue.text: Tease Jack, perhaps

definitions.meaning: to comb out wool fibres is to tease them
the jack is one of the court ... in a pack

explanation.definitionFit: Teasing wool with a toothed comb is carding it, and a jack is a playing card.

clue.text: Inspector cut back one of Thatcher's targets?

indicators.note: the word is read backwards

parts.note: to axe is to cut
Margaret Thatcher's government fought the coal miners in the 1984-85 strike

explanation.surface: An official reviewing the cuts made to a group Thatcher opposed.
explanation.walkthrough: Margaret Thatcher, UK prime minister in the 1980s, defeated the National Union of Mineworkers in a year-long strike.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who inspects or tests, such as an exam marker, is an inspector.

clue.text: I don't know — Manchester banning books before revision

indicators.note: revising the remaining letters puts them in a new order
the books are excluded from the city's letters

parts.note: NT is the New Testament, a set of books of the Bible

explanation.surface: A shrug about whether Manchester banned books before revising its rules.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revision' shuffles MACHESER, Manchester without NT.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiomatic reply meaning you have no idea, inviting the asker to look in your pockets.

clue.text: Work around man who has cleared out tenement where the poor live

indicators.note: the work word goes around the other letters

parts.note: to go is to work or function
he refers to a man

indicators.note: a cleared-out word loses its middle, leaving only its ends

explanation.surface: A man clears out a block of flats where the poor live.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cleared out' sounds like an eviction but empties 'tenement' to TT.
explanation.definitionFit: A deprived, overcrowded urban district housing a minority or the poor.
